title: GI bleeding and abdominal emergencies
summary: GI emergencies in the ICU: variceal and non-variceal upper GI bleeding with Glasgow-Blatchford, severe acute pancreatitis, intra-abdominal hypertension and compartment syndrome, acute mesenteric ischaemia, and ileus/colonic pseudo-obstruction.

topics.title: Acute variceal bleeding
topics.summary: Baveno VII bundle: restrictive transfusion, vasoactive drug, antibiotics, endoscopy within 12 h, pre-emptive TIPS, and rescue options.

definition.text: Suspect variceal bleeding in any patient with cirrhosis or portal hypertension and UGIB. Mortality 10-20% at 6 weeks; highest in Child-Pugh C and with ACLF.

steps.title: Resuscitate and protect airway
steps.detail: Two large-bore IVs, cautious volume replacement; intubate for massive haematemesis, encephalopathy (GCS ≤ 8) or before endoscopy if airway at risk.

steps.title: Restrictive transfusion
steps.detail: Transfuse PRBC at Hb ≤ 7 g/dL, target 7-8 g/dL (higher if active cardiovascular disease or massive bleeding). Do not correct INR with FFP; platelets/fibrinogen per clinical judgement.

steps.title: Vasoactive drug immediately
steps.detail: Terlipressin 2 mg IV q4h (or octreotide 50 mcg bolus + 50 mcg/h) as soon as variceal bleed suspected, before endoscopy; continue 2-5 days.

steps.title: Antibiotic prophylaxis
steps.detail: Ceftriaxone 1 g/day IV for up to 7 days (reduces infection, rebleeding and death).

steps.title: Endoscopy within 12 h
steps.detail: After resuscitation; erythromycin 250 mg IV 30-120 min before improves visibility. Band ligation for oesophageal varices; cyanoacrylate glue for gastric (GOV2/IGV1) varices.

steps.title: Pre-emptive TIPS
steps.detail: Child-Pugh C 10-13 or Child B > 7 with active bleeding at endoscopy: pre-emptive TIPS within 72 h (ideally < 24 h) if available.

steps.title: Refractory bleeding
steps.detail: Balloon tamponade (Sengstaken-Blakemore/Minnesota, max 24 h) or self-expanding oesophageal stent as bridge to rescue TIPS.

steps.title: Prevent complications
steps.detail: Lactulose/rifaximin to prevent encephalopathy, avoid nephrotoxins, start non-selective beta-blocker after vasoactive drugs stop (secondary prophylaxis) with repeat EVL.

doseCards.dose: 2 mg q4h for 48 h, then 1 mg q4h; total 2-5 days
doseCards.workedExample: Start 2 mg IV immediately; reduce to 1 mg q4h once bleeding controlled

doseCards.dose: 1 g once daily up to 7 days
250 mg over 30 min, 30-120 min before endoscopy

redFlags.text: Haematemesis with encephalopathy or haemodynamic instability: intubate before endoscopy to prevent aspiration.
Rebleeding within 5 days or failure to control: rescue TIPS or balloon tamponade/stent.

pitfalls.text: Over-transfusion to Hb > 9-10 g/dL raises portal pressure and rebleeding.
Giving FFP to correct INR before endoscopy: INR does not reflect bleeding risk in cirrhosis and FFP raises portal pressure.

pearls.text: Start terlipressin and antibiotics in the ED; do not wait for endoscopy.

nodes.text: IV access; transfuse if Hb ≤ 7 (target 7-8); no FFP for INR
Child C 10-13 or B > 7 with active bleeding?
Vasoactive 2-5 days, lactulose, then NSBB + repeat EVL

consultantNotes.pathophysiology: Portal hypertension (HVPG ≥ 10 mmHg) opens portosystemic collaterals; varices bleed when HVPG > 12 mmHg and wall tension exceeds strength. Volume overload and splanchnic vasodilation raise portal pressure, which is why restrictive transfusion and vasoconstrictors help.
consultantNotes.evidence:
- Baveno VII (2022): restrictive transfusion, vasoactive drugs, antibiotic prophylaxis, endoscopy within 12 h, pre-emptive TIPS in high-risk patients [de Franchis 2022].
- Restrictive transfusion (Hb 7) reduced mortality and rebleeding compared with liberal (Hb 9) [Villanueva 2013].
consultantNotes.controversies: - Pre-emptive TIPS selection criteria and availability; role of TXA (HALT-IT showed no benefit and more VTE).
consultantNotes.indiaNotes:
- Terlipressin and EVL are widely available in India; TIPS is limited to tertiary centres (ILBS, AIIMS, large private hospitals).
- Alcohol, hepatitis B and NASH (MASLD) are main causes of cirrhosis; extrahepatic portal vein obstruction and non-cirrhotic portal fibrosis cause variceal bleeds in younger Indians with preserved liver function.

topics.title: Non-variceal UGIB and Glasgow-Blatchford
topics.summary: Risk-stratify with Glasgow-Blatchford, resuscitate, give PPI, time endoscopy, and manage rebleeding and anticoagulants.

definition.text: Non-variceal UGIB is mostly peptic ulcer (H. pylori, NSAIDs/aspirin), erosive disease, Mallory-Weiss, malignancy, Dieulafoy. Glasgow-Blatchford score (GBS) 0-1 = very low risk (outpatient management possible).

steps.title: Assess and resuscitate
steps.detail: Haemodynamics, shock index, Hb, urea, INR, cross-match. Restrictive transfusion: Hb ≤ 7 g/dL (target 7-9); Hb ≤ 8 (target ≥ 10) with cardiovascular disease.

steps.title: Calculate GBS
steps.detail: Blood urea, Hb, SBP, pulse ≥ 100, melaena, syncope, hepatic disease, cardiac failure. GBS ≤ 1: consider outpatient endoscopy. Higher scores: admit.

steps.title: PPI
steps.detail: High-dose IV PPI (pantoprazole 80 mg bolus) before endoscopy; do not delay endoscopy for it.

steps.title: Anticoagulants and antiplatelets
steps.detail: Hold anticoagulants; reverse if life-threatening (vitamin K + PCC for warfarin; idarucizumab for dabigatran; PCC/andexanet for Xa inhibitors). Continue aspirin for secondary prevention if possible; discuss DAPT with cardiology.

steps.title: Endoscopy within 24 h
steps.detail: After resuscitation, within 24 h. Very early endoscopy (< 6-12 h) did not improve outcome in high-risk patients (Lau 2020) unless unstable despite resuscitation.

steps.title: Post-endoscopy
steps.detail: High-risk stigmata (Forrest Ia, Ib, IIa, IIb) treated endoscopically: high-dose PPI for 72 h (continuous or intermittent 40 mg BD), then oral BD to 2 weeks; test and treat H. pylori.

steps.title: Rebleeding
steps.detail: Repeat endoscopy; if fails: transcatheter arterial embolisation (TAE) or surgery.

steps.title: Do not use TXA
steps.detail: HALT-IT: high-dose TXA did not reduce death and increased venous thromboembolism.

doseCards.dose: 80 mg bolus, then 8 mg/h for 72 h (or 40 mg IV BD) after endotherapy

tables.title: Glasgow-Blatchford score
tables.caption: Original score uses blood urea in mmol/L. Indian labs usually report urea in mg/dL (mmol/L × 6); US labs report BUN (mmol/L × 2.8). Use the matching column.

redFlags.text: Shock index > 1, haematemesis of fresh blood, or Hb drop ≥ 2 g/dL: high-risk bleed - ICU/HDU, early endoscopy after resuscitation.

pitfalls.text: Delaying resuscitation for endoscopy, or endoscoping an unresuscitated patient.
Stopping aspirin permanently in a patient with coronary stents: thrombosis risk; restart early (often within 3-5 days) after discussion.

pearls.text: Forrest classification: Ia spurting, Ib oozing, IIa visible vessel, IIb adherent clot, IIc flat spot, III clean base.

nodes.text: Resuscitate, restrictive transfusion, PPI 80 mg, ICU
Oral PPI, H. pylori test and treat, early feeding

consultantNotes.pathophysiology: Acid impairs platelet aggregation and dissolves clot; maintaining intragastric pH > 6 with PPIs stabilises clot over an ulcer after endoscopic haemostasis.
consultantNotes.evidence:
- ESGE 2021: GBS ≤ 1 for outpatient management; restrictive transfusion; endoscopy within 24 h; high-dose PPI after endotherapy [Gralnek 2021].
- Lau 2020 (516 high-risk patients): endoscopy within 6 h did not reduce 30-day mortality compared with 6-24 h [Lau 2020].
- HALT-IT (12,009 patients): TXA no benefit, more VTE [HALT-IT 2020].
consultantNotes.controversies: - Over-the-scope clips as first-line for high-risk ulcers; haemostatic powders.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes:
- NSAID overuse (over-the-counter) and H. pylori are common causes; check also for portal hypertension even without known cirrhosis.
- Blood urea in India is reported as urea (mg/dL), not BUN; convert carefully when scoring.

topics.title: Severe acute pancreatitis
topics.summary: Diagnose and grade by revised Atlanta, moderate fluids (WATERFALL), early enteral feeding, no prophylactic antibiotics, and the step-up approach to infected necrosis.

definition.text: Acute pancreatitis = 2 of 3: typical pain, lipase/amylase > 3x upper limit, imaging findings. Severity (revised Atlanta): mild (no organ failure/complications), moderately severe (transient organ failure < 48 h and/or local/systemic complications), severe (persistent organ failure > 48 h by modified Marshall score).

steps.title: Confirm and find the cause
steps.detail: Lipase (or amylase), USG abdomen for gallstones, triglycerides (> 1,000 mg/dL), calcium, alcohol history, drugs, ERCP/trauma. CT only if diagnosis uncertain or deterioration after 72-96 h.

steps.title: Predict severity
steps.detail: BISAP (BUN > 25 mg/dL, i.e. urea > 53 mg/dL, impaired mental status, SIRS, age > 60, pleural effusion; ≥ 3 = high risk), SIRS persisting > 48 h, haematocrit, urea trend; monitor organ failure (modified Marshall).

steps.title: Moderate, goal-directed fluids
steps.detail: Ringer lactate: 10 mL/kg bolus if hypovolaemic, then 1.5 mL/kg/h; reassess at 3, 12, 24, 48, 72 h. Avoid aggressive fluids (WATERFALL: more overload, no benefit).

steps.title: Analgesia
steps.detail: Paracetamol + opioids (fentanyl/morphine as needed); epidural in selected patients.

steps.title: Feed early
steps.detail: Oral diet as tolerated within 24-72 h; if not tolerated, enteral via nasogastric or nasojejunal tube (equivalent). Avoid TPN unless enteral fails.

steps.title: Antibiotics only for infection
steps.detail: No prophylactic antibiotics in sterile necrosis. Suspect infected necrosis if deterioration/fever after 7-10 days or gas in necrosis on CT: carbapenem/quinolone + metronidazole, FNA if unclear.

steps.title: Biliary: ERCP if cholangitis
steps.detail: Urgent ERCP (< 24 h) for cholangitis; not routinely for gallstone pancreatitis without obstruction. Cholecystectomy in same admission for mild biliary pancreatitis.

steps.title: Step-up for infected necrosis
steps.detail: Antibiotics first; delay intervention ≥ 4 weeks (walled-off necrosis) if possible; percutaneous or endoscopic drainage, then minimally invasive necrosectomy if needed. Monitor IAP.

doseCards.dose: 10 mL/kg bolus if hypovolaemic, then 1.5 mL/kg/h
doseCards.workedExample: 70 kg, hypovolaemic: 700 mL bolus, then 105 mL/h; reassess at 3 h (stop at 48 h if tolerating oral)

tables.title: Revised Atlanta severity
rows: Local (collections, necrosis) or exacerbation of comorbidity

redFlags.text: Persistent organ failure > 48 h, rising IAP > 20 mmHg, or fever with clinical deterioration after the first week (infected necrosis): ICU and specialist pancreatic team.

pitfalls.text: Early CT on day 1 underestimates necrosis and rarely changes management.
Keeping patients 'nil by mouth to rest the pancreas': early feeding reduces infection and mortality.

pearls.text: Hypertriglyceridaemia-induced pancreatitis: insulin infusion (with dextrose) lowers TG; plasmapheresis in selected cases.

nodes.text: Assess organ failure (Marshall), BISAP, SIRS; USG for gallstones
ICU: CT at 72-96 h, IAP monitoring, step-up if infected necrosis
Ward care; cholecystectomy same admission if biliary

consultantNotes.pathophysiology: Premature activation of trypsin within acinar cells causes autodigestion, local inflammation and a systemic inflammatory response with capillary leak, leading to organ failure. Necrosis may become infected (translocation) usually after the first week.
consultantNotes.evidence:
- WATERFALL (2022): aggressive vs moderate LR resuscitation - more fluid overload (20.5% vs 6.3%) without improving outcomes; stopped early [de-Madaria 2022].
- PANTER (2010): step-up approach reduced major complications or death vs open necrosectomy [van Santvoort 2010].
- ACG 2024 guideline: moderate fluids, early oral feeding, no prophylactic antibiotics, delayed intervention for necrosis [Tenner 2024].
consultantNotes.controversies: - Optimal fluid in severe pancreatitis already in organ failure (WATERFALL excluded these).
consultantNotes.indiaNotes:
- Alcohol is the leading cause in Indian men, gallstones in women; tropical (idiopathic) chronic pancreatitis is a regional entity.
- Endoscopic necrosectomy expertise exists at major Indian centres (e.g. AIG Hyderabad).

topics.title: Intra-abdominal hypertension and compartment syndrome
topics.summary: Measure IAP correctly, grade IAH, and treat ACS with the WSACS stepwise approach up to decompressive laparotomy.

definition.text: IAH = sustained IAP ≥ 12 mmHg (grade I 12-15, II 16-20, III 21-25, IV > 25). Abdominal compartment syndrome = sustained IAP > 20 mmHg with new organ dysfunction. APP = MAP - IAP (target ≥ 60 mmHg).

steps.title: Who to measure
steps.detail: Two or more risk factors: massive fluid resuscitation/positive balance, massive transfusion, pancreatitis, abdominal surgery/trauma, ileus, ascites, burns, prone position, high PEEP, obesity, sepsis.

steps.title: Measure via bladder
steps.detail: Supine, end-expiration, transducer zeroed at mid-axillary line at iliac crest, instil ≤ 25 mL sterile saline, wait 30-60 s, read in mmHg. Repeat 4-6 hourly in IAH.

steps.title: Evacuate intraluminal contents
steps.detail: Nasogastric and rectal decompression, prokinetics, enemas, endoscopic decompression.

steps.title: Evacuate intra-abdominal fluid
steps.detail: Percutaneous drainage of ascites/collections (ultrasound-guided).

steps.title: Improve wall compliance
steps.detail: Adequate analgesia/sedation, avoid head-up > 30°, remove tight dressings/binders, neuromuscular blockade trial for refractory cases.

steps.title: Optimise fluids
steps.detail: Avoid positive fluid balance after initial resuscitation; diuretics or ultrafiltration (RRT); use hypertonic/colloid if appropriate.

steps.title: Decompressive laparotomy
steps.detail: For refractory ACS with organ dysfunction; temporary abdominal closure (vacuum).

redFlags.text: Rising airway pressures, oliguria and falling cardiac output in a tense distended abdomen: measure IAP now.

pitfalls.text: Measuring IAP with the patient head-up, with active abdominal muscle contraction, or using > 25 mL saline: falsely high.
Treating oliguria from ACS with more fluid boluses.

pearls.text: Clinical examination of abdominal tension is unreliable; measure.

nodes.text: Medical steps: NG/rectal decompression, drain fluid, sedation/analgesia, avoid positive balance
IAP > 20 with new organ dysfunction despite medical therapy?
Continue measures; IAP 4-6 hourly; target APP ≥ 60

consultantNotes.pathophysiology: Raised IAP compresses the IVC (reducing venous return), splints the diaphragm (reducing compliance, raising airway pressures), compresses renal veins and parenchyma (oliguria) and reduces splanchnic perfusion, causing gut ischaemia and further oedema.
consultantNotes.evidence: - WSACS 2013 consensus definitions and stepwise medical/surgical management algorithm [Kirkpatrick 2013].
consultantNotes.controversies: - Optimal APP target; prophylactic open abdomen in damage-control surgery.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes: - IAP measurement needs only a urinary catheter, a three-way tap and a transducer (or manometer): cheap and feasible in all Indian ICUs.

topics.title: Acute mesenteric ischaemia
topics.summary: High suspicion, immediate CT angiography, heparin, antibiotics and urgent revascularisation or laparotomy.

definition.text: Acute mesenteric ischaemia (AMI): arterial embolism (~50%, often AF), arterial thrombosis (atherosclerosis), non-occlusive (NOMI, low-flow shock, vasopressors) or mesenteric venous thrombosis. Mortality 50-80%; time is bowel.

steps.title: Suspect
steps.detail: Severe abdominal pain out of proportion to examination, AF, recent MI, vasculopathy, shock on vasopressors, hypercoagulable states; later peritonitis, bloody stools, rising lactate.

steps.title: CT angiography immediately
steps.detail: Biphasic CTA as soon as suspected; do not delay for creatinine. Lactate and D-dimer are not sensitive enough to exclude.

steps.title: Start treatment
steps.detail: Fluid resuscitation, UFH 80 units/kg bolus then infusion (unless contraindicated), broad-spectrum antibiotics, NG decompression, analgesia.

steps.title: Revascularise
steps.detail: Arterial occlusion: endovascular (thrombectomy, stent) or open embolectomy/bypass; laparotomy if peritonitis to resect non-viable bowel; planned second-look at 24-48 h.

steps.title: NOMI
steps.detail: Treat cause of low flow, minimise vasoconstrictors, optimise cardiac output; intra-arterial vasodilator (papaverine) in specialist centres; laparotomy if peritonitis.

steps.title: Venous thrombosis
steps.detail: Therapeutic anticoagulation; surgery if infarction; investigate thrombophilia/malignancy.

doseCards.workedExample: 70 kg: 5,600 units bolus, then 1,260 units/h = 2.5 mL/h

redFlags.text: Unexplained metabolic acidosis/lactate rise in a ventilated patient on vasopressors with feed intolerance or distension: think NOMI.

pitfalls.text: A normal lactate does not exclude early AMI.
Delaying CTA because of AKI risk from contrast.

pearls.text: Bowel viability can be underestimated at first operation; a second-look laparotomy is standard after revascularisation.

nodes.text: Immediate CT angiography; fluids, heparin, antibiotics
Arterial occlusion: endovascular or open revascularisation
Venous thrombosis: anticoagulate; surgery if infarction
NOMI: improve flow, reduce vasopressors, consider vasodilator

consultantNotes.pathophysiology: The mucosa is most sensitive to ischaemia (villus tips); necrosis progresses transmurally over 6-12 h, with bacterial translocation, sepsis and perforation.
consultantNotes.evidence: - WSES 2022 guidelines: CTA without delay, systemic heparin, revascularisation and damage-control surgery [Bala 2022].
consultantNotes.controversies: - Endovascular-first vs open-first strategy; role of hybrid suites.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes: - Rheumatic heart disease with AF is an important embolic source in younger Indians; venous mesenteric thrombosis is associated with hypercoagulable states and cirrhosis.

topics.title: Ileus and acute colonic pseudo-obstruction
topics.summary: Recognise ICU ileus, exclude mechanical obstruction, correct causes, and treat Ogilvie syndrome with neostigmine or decompression.

definition.text: Ileus = functional impairment of gut motility without mechanical obstruction (post-operative, sepsis, opioids, electrolytes). Acute colonic pseudo-obstruction (Ogilvie) = massive colonic dilatation without obstruction; caecal diameter > 10-12 cm raises perforation risk.

steps.title: Exclude mechanical obstruction
steps.detail: Examine hernias and scars; abdominal X-ray and CT (transition point, volvulus, closed loop) if any doubt.

steps.title: Correct contributors
steps.detail: Keep K > 4 mmol/L and Mg > 2 mg/dL, correct phosphate and glucose; reduce opioids (multimodal analgesia), stop anticholinergics, treat sepsis, mobilise early.

steps.title: Decompress
steps.detail: Nasogastric tube for vomiting/gastric distension; rectal tube; avoid feeding into a distended dilated stomach (trickle feeds once tolerated).

steps.title: Prokinetics
steps.detail: Metoclopramide 10 mg IV q8h (upper GI), erythromycin 250 mg IV q8h; for opioid-induced constipation consider methylnaltrexone (where available) or laxatives.

steps.title: Ogilvie: neostigmine
steps.detail: If caecum > 10 cm or no improvement after 24-48 h conservative care and no contraindication: neostigmine 2 mg IV over 3-5 min with cardiac monitoring and atropine ready; patient supine on bedpan.

steps.title: Colonoscopic decompression or surgery
steps.detail: If neostigmine fails/contraindicated: colonoscopic decompression ± tube; surgery for perforation, ischaemia or failure.

steps.title: Monitor IAP
steps.detail: Severe distension can cause IAH/ACS.

doseCards.dose: 2 mg over 3-5 min; repeat once if needed
doseCards.workedExample: 2 mg (4 mL of 0.5 mg/mL) slow IV with ECG monitoring; atropine 0.6 mg drawn up
doseCards.notes: Expect evacuation within 30 min in responders.

redFlags.text: Caecal diameter > 12 cm, tenderness, fever or peritonism in pseudo-obstruction: risk of perforation - urgent surgical review.

pitfalls.text: Giving neostigmine before excluding mechanical obstruction.

pearls.text: Most neostigmine responders pass flatus or stool within 30 minutes; recurrence occurs in a minority and a second dose may be given.

nodes.text: Correct K/Mg/PO4, reduce opioids, NG/rectal tube, mobilise
Colonic dilatation, caecum > 10 cm or no response at 48 h?
Neostigmine 2 mg IV with monitoring (if no contraindication)

consultantNotes.pathophysiology: Sympathetic overactivity, inflammation, opioids and electrolyte disturbances inhibit propulsive motility. In Ogilvie syndrome, autonomic imbalance (reduced parasympathetic tone) dilates the colon; by Laplace's law the caecum, with the largest diameter, has the highest wall tension.
consultantNotes.evidence: - Ponec 1999 RCT: neostigmine produced prompt decompression in 10/11 patients vs 0/10 with placebo [Ponec 1999].
consultantNotes.controversies: - Neostigmine infusion vs bolus; prophylactic PEG/osmotic laxatives after decompression.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes: - Methylnaltrexone and alvimopan are not widely available in India; neostigmine and colonoscopy are the practical options.

drugs.name: Terlipressin
drugs.adultDose: 2 mg IV every 4 h until bleeding controlled (first 48 h), then 1 mg every 4 h; continue 2-5 days.
drugs.preparationIndia: 1 mg vials; give as IV bolus.
drugs.cautions: Ischaemia (cardiac, mesenteric, digital), hyponatraemia, bradycardia; avoid in significant IHD/PVD.

drugs.name: Octreotide
drugs.adultDose: 50 mcg IV bolus, then 50 mcg/h infusion for 2-5 days.
drugs.preparationIndia: 100 mcg/mL ampoules; 500 mcg in 50 mL NS = 10 mcg/mL (5 mL/h = 50 mcg/h).

drugs.name: Ceftriaxone
drugs.indications: Antibiotic prophylaxis in cirrhosis with GI bleeding
drugs.adultDose: 1 g IV once daily for up to 7 days.
drugs.cautions: Choose per local resistance (e.g. if high ESBL rates).

drugs.name: Erythromycin
drugs.adultDose: 250 mg IV over 30 min, 30-120 min before endoscopy.
drugs.preparationIndia: IV erythromycin lactobionate has limited availability in India.
drugs.verify: IV erythromycin may be unavailable in many Indian hospitals.

drugs.name: Pantoprazole (or esomeprazole)
drugs.adultDose: Pre-endoscopy: 80 mg IV bolus. After endoscopic therapy of high-risk ulcer: 80 mg bolus then 8 mg/h for 72 h, or 40 mg IV twice daily (intermittent high dose, non-inferior); then oral twice daily to complete 2 weeks.
drugs.preparationIndia: 40 mg vials; infusion 80 mg in 100 mL NS (0.8 mg/mL) at 10 mL/h = 8 mg/h.

drugs.name: Ringer lactate
drugs.adultDose: Hypovolaemic: 10 mL/kg bolus, then 1.5 mL/kg/h; reassess at 3, 12, 24, 48 and 72 h (WATERFALL moderate strategy). Not hypovolaemic: 1.5 mL/kg/h without bolus.
drugs.cautions: Aggressive fluids (20 mL/kg bolus + 3 mL/kg/h) increased fluid overload without benefit.

drugs.name: Unfractionated heparin
drugs.adultDose: 80 units/kg IV bolus, then 18 units/kg/h titrated to aPTT 1.5-2.5x control.

drugs.name: Neostigmine
drugs.indications: Acute colonic pseudo-obstruction (Ogilvie) not responding to conservative care
drugs.adultDose: 2 mg IV over 3-5 min with cardiac monitoring; may repeat once. Atropine 0.6-1 mg at bedside for bradycardia.
drugs.cautions: Contraindicated in mechanical obstruction, perforation, recent bowel anastomosis, bradycardia, active bronchospasm.
